problem:
Consider the solid enclosed between the paraboloid $x=-2+{y}^{2}+4{z}^{2}$ and the parabolic cylinder $x=-1+2{z}^{2},$ whose volume can be written in terms of double integrals, as follows:

$$
V={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{a(y)}^{b(y)}\,f(y,z)\,dz\,dy
$$

What is ${a}^{2}+{b}^{2}+f?$
worked_solution:
First, we need to determine the projection of the intersection of our surfaces onto the $yz$-plane. So, let's find where they intersect.

$$
\begin{aligned}-2+{y}^{2}+4{z}^{2} & =-1+2{z}^{2} \\ {y}^{2}+2{z}^{2} & =1 \\ {y}^{2}+2{z}^{2} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

So, the projection of the intersection in the $yz$-plane is an ellipse.

Notice that our solid can be written as a type II region: 

$$
R={(x,y,z)\,:\,(y,z)\in D,\,\,-2+{y}^{2}+4{z}^{2}\le x\le -1+2{z}^{2}},
$$

where $D$ is the interior of the ellipse ${y}^{2}+2{z}^{2}=1.$ 

As a result, the volume of $R$ is given by 

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={∭}_{R}\text{d}V \\  & ={∬}_{D}[{\int }_{-2+{y}^{2}+4{z}^{2}}^{-1+2{z}^{2}}\text{d}x]\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-1+2{z}^{2})-(-2+{y}^{2}+4{z}^{2})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}1-{y}^{2}-2{z}^{2}\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, notice that the boundary of $D$ consists of 

- the lower part $z=-\sqrt{\frac{1-{y}^{2}}{2}},$ and

- the upper part $z=\sqrt{\frac{1-{y}^{2}}{2}},$

for $-1\le y\le 1.$ 

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}1-{y}^{2}-2{z}^{2}\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{-\sqrt{(1-{y}^{2})/2}}^{\sqrt{(1-{y}^{2})/2}}\,1-{y}^{2}-2{z}^{2}\,dz\,dy.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}^{2}+{b}^{2}+f & ={(-\sqrt{\frac{1-{y}^{2}}{2}})}^{2}+{(\sqrt{\frac{1-{y}^{2}}{2}})}^{2}+(1-{y}^{2}-2{z}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{1-{y}^{2}}{2}+\frac{1-{y}^{2}}{2}+(1-{y}^{2}-2{z}^{2}) \\  & =2-2{y}^{2}-2{z}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
